## Glossary {#glossary}

The four terms below follow the definitions in @NosekEtAl2025BriefGlossaryTerms. They are not interchangeable, and the course depends on the difference: a finding can survive every robustness check on its own data and still fail on new data, or survive the checks and still be one that nobody can recompute from the original materials. The column 'In this course' notes where each idea appears in the EU-frames case.

| Term | Definition | In this course |
|------------------------|------------------------|------------------------|
| **Reproducibility** | Same question, same data, same analysis → same result | Tested across the SCORE sample by @MiskeEtAl2026InvestigatingReproducibilitySocial. In the EU-frames case, the result reported by the original author (OA) was not reproducible from the original materials, and the class reproduces in Task 3 a value that Multi100 recorded for one of the analysts |
| **Robustness** | Same question, same data, justifiable alternative analysis → stable result | The Multi100 design [@AczelEtAl2026InvestigatingAnalyticalRobustness]; the five analysts of the claim; the specification menu and the curve of the claim in Tasks 4 and 5, with 864 specifications |
| **Replicability** | Same question, independent new data → same result | Tested across the SCORE sample by @TynerEtAl2026InvestigatingReplicabilitySocial. For the EU-frames claim, a replication on later Eurobarometer waves was judged not successful |
| **Repeatability** | Umbrella term covering all three above | Used in the glossary of Nosek and colleagues as the overarching category |

### The SCORE dossier {#the-eu-frames-case-score-dossier-one-paper-all-three-rs}

The target article [@Teney2016DoesEUEconomic] was put through all three SCORE activities, and the three reached three different verdicts on the same paper: the reproduction failed twice, in different ways, the robustness reanalysis by the five Multi100 analysts held in sign while its recorded effect sizes ran from −0.006 to −0.452, and the preregistered replication on later Eurobarometer waves was judged not successful (first report b = +0.002, p = .046, N = 352,114; revised report of October 2026 b = +0.001, SE 0.0007, t = 1.428, p = 0.153, N = 331,668). The parent node of the dossier is <https://osf.io/h7432/>; the [repositories module](companion/repositories.qmd#sec-trail-eu-frames) sets out its components node by node, and the [case study](cases/eu-frames/index.qmd#sec-repetition) tells the story in full.

## Core readings

### The three *Nature* 2026 papers (SCORE)

- **Reproducibility:** @MiskeEtAl2026InvestigatingReproducibilitySocial – how often the central result of a paper can be recomputed from its own data. <https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-026-10203-5>
- **Robustness:** @AczelEtAl2026InvestigatingAnalyticalRobustness – Multi100, in which at least five analysts reanalysed each of a hundred claims. <https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-025-09844-9>
- **Replicability:** @TynerEtAl2026InvestigatingReplicabilitySocial – how often claims hold on new data, under preregistered protocols. <https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-025-10078-y>
- @AlipourfardEtAl2021SystematizingConfidenceOpen – the SCORE programme, of which all three studies are part. <https://doi.org/10.31235/osf.io/46mnb>

### Vocabulary

- @NosekEtAl2025BriefGlossaryTerms – a four-page glossary of the terms of repeatability; read it before the day. <https://doi.org/10.31222/osf.io/mqfp4_v1>
- @NosekErrington2020WhatReplication – what counts as a replication. <https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pbio.3000691>

### Estimands and analytical choices

- @LundbergEtAl2021WhatYourEstimand – the steps from a theoretical estimand to an empirical one, and why a result means little until the estimand is stated. <https://doi.org/10.1177/00031224211004187>
- @SilberzahnEtAl2018ManyAnalystsOne – the red-card study, in which twenty-nine teams analysed one dataset. <https://doi.org/10.1177/2515245917747646>
- @AuspurgBruderl2021HasCredibilitySocial – the reanalysis of the red-card study that traced the spread of its results to teams answering different questions. <https://doi.org/10.1177/23780231211024421>

### The multiverse and its critics

- @SimmonsEtAl2011FalsePositivePsychology and @GelmanLoken2014StatisticalCrisisScience – how undisclosed flexibility in analysis produces false positives, and the garden of forking paths.
- @SteegenEtAl2016IncreasingTransparencyMultiverse and @SimonsohnEtAl2020SpecificationCurveAnalysis – the multiverse analysis and the specification curve, the two proposals on which the curve of the claim draws.
- @DelGiudiceGangestad2021TravelersGuideMultiverse – a systematic framework for judging which analytic decisions are equivalent, and so which analyses belong in one multiverse.
- @BreznauEtAl2022ObservingManyResearchers – a many-analysts study in which teams tested one hypothesis about immigration and social policy on the same data.
- @Auspurg2025RobustnessBetterAssessed – the case for a few thoughtful models over billions of regressions.
- @RohrerEtAl2026WhatsMultiverseGood and @LakensEtAl2026ThereOnlyOne – what a multiverse is good for, and the argument that a fully specified question has only one correct analysis.
- @HeymanVanpaemel2022MultiverseAnalysesClassroom – the multiverse as a teaching device.
- [Reading a specification curve](cases/eu-frames/reading-inference.qmd) – the course reading for the final part of the EU-frames day: why a large set of results is not a large set of independent tests, and what a single test across the whole curve can and cannot establish.

The [companion module on the multiverse](companion/multiverse.qmd) reads these against the curve of the claim.

### Preregistration

None of these is required, because everything is taught in the course, but they let you arrive with the ideas already in hand. All three are open access.

- Nosek, Ebersole, DeHaven & Mellor (2018). The preregistration revolution. *PNAS*, 115(11), 2600–2606. <https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.1708274114> – a short primer on the idea on which preregistration depends: predicting a result against explaining one after the fact, and the case, like ours, where the data already exist.
- The AsPredicted eight-question form – the short template on which the preregistration block of your report is modelled, listed on the OSF as the "Preregistration Template from AsPredicted.org". Live form: <https://aspredicted.org>; OSF listing: <https://help.osf.io/article/158-create-a-preregistration>.
- van den Akker, Weston, Campbell, et al. (2021). Preregistration of secondary data analysis: A template and tutorial. *Meta-Psychology*, 5, 2625. <https://doi.org/10.15626/MP.2020.2625> – the fuller template, built for our situation of reanalysing data that already exist, and the tool that a full version of the exercise would use.

## Companion

The modules of the [companion](companion/index.qmd) hold the teaching that a single day can only mention, each written on the data of this case, and the companion index lists them with a line on each. Installing R and an IDE, the setup help, and the modules on the tools, from [Getting started with R](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/tools/r.html) to [Quarto documents](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/tools/quarto.html) and [Git and GitHub](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/git-github.html), are on the [AR4DS site](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/), which every case shares.

## If you are at Newcastle University

The course is open to anyone, and support of the kind listed below exists wherever you are: the library at your own institution and its research-software or research-data team are the places to ask. As an example, participants based at Newcastle University can draw on the following.

| Resource | URL |
|------------------------------------|------------------------------------|
| RSE training (Research Software Engineering) | <https://rse.ncldata.dev/events> |
| NCL Library – open research pages | <https://www.ncl.ac.uk/library/academic-support/research/open-research/> |
| Research Data Newcastle | <https://data.ncl.ac.uk> |
| UKRN Primers (open research primers) | <https://www.ukrn.org/primers/> |
| ReproducibiliTea Newcastle | Search 'ReproducibiliTea Newcastle' – a journal club for open and reproducible science |
